scope: Independent visual craft and recruiter scanning review of all eight full, uncropped native iPhone 17 / iOS 26.5 screenshots. Synthetic content. No source, other review, plan, or Simulator inspection. Still images establish appearance only.
scenario: An independent recruiter juggling several live searches needs to find and reopen the correct person or conversation, identify context and recency, and distinguish unread content from review-needed work.

categories.assessment: Default-size topics and names are a clear first read, with quiet secondary context and recency. The AX5 shell substantially delays that first read, and the two attention states are not self-explanatory.
Default English and Chinese dark UI are readable with useful hierarchy. Essential navigation labels and the person's surname do not survive AX5 gracefully.
Normal row insets, separators, and sparse content are coherent. AX5 introduces awkward grouping and a large utility row before the first result. Large content scrolling is not itself penalized.
Warm neutral surfaces, sparse elevation, and the lack of row chevrons are restrained. The composer treatment becomes disproportionately prominent, especially at AX5.

Both pages share search, filter, selected-page underline, and menu placement. The visible active People scope has a clear removal affordance, and dark variants remain readable. The common shell has not adapted coherently to AX5.

deductions.observation: The result count and Synthetic preview expand into a dominant utility band; the large Ask anything composer occupies much of the bottom viewport. The first result begins substantially farther down the screen than at normal size, and its context and recency are not visible together in the captured viewport.
deductions.impact: A short retrieval scan starts with utility copy and generic input chrome before the relationship context. This is an observed hierarchy cost, not proof that scrolled content is inaccessible.

deductions.observation: The first session keeps the same Review needed label in the light read/unread pair; the material change is the only visible cue to unread state. No row label identifies that surface treatment as unread.
deductions.impact: A recruiter seeing only the unread screenshot can reasonably associate the raised row with review-needed work. The states are technically rendered differently but not independently self-explanatory.

deductions.observation: Leila's identity shares the immediate context line with the search, while Nia's identity appears on a smaller bottom metadata line after Board search.
deductions.impact: Name scanning across session rows requires checking different positions and levels of emphasis.

deductions.observation: The navigation visibly truncates Sessions and People to Ses... and Peo... while Today remains complete.
deductions.impact: Essential destination labels are incomplete at the selected accessibility text size.

deductions.observation: The first person's name wraps as Leila / Hart- / mann in the narrow name area beside the initials.
deductions.impact: A surname, the central retrieval identifier, is broken inside the word despite the availability of a full-width row layout.

deductions.observation: The active-filter result count reads 1 people.
deductions.impact: A visible singular-count grammar defect weakens the otherwise deliberate label treatment.

deductions.observation: The initials circle is centered against a three-line name, followed by full-width role/company text starting at the outer inset.
deductions.impact: The row changes its grouping axis mid-record; the compact initials occupy a lane that no longer helps align identity and context.

deductions.observation: The count and Synthetic preview remain two large side-by-side blocks. Preview wraps to two lines, and the Sessions count also wraps, creating a tall metadata band before the first result.
deductions.impact: Utility metadata has a loose, oversized rhythm relative to its supporting role. The honest blank space after the two normal-size rows receives no deduction.

deductions.observation: The keyboard, composer plus, and waveform glyphs become extremely large and heavy while row ellipses remain small.
deductions.impact: Generic shell commands acquire visual weight comparable to the primary identity or topic and compete with retrieval content.

deductions.observation: The pale composer has a bright outline and broad shadow across the otherwise very quiet lower viewport.
deductions.impact: This repeated elevation draws more attention to generic input than is useful for the reviewed retrieval task. This is a minor craft judgment, not an argument to remove the command.

deductions.observation: Both accessibility captures retain the same single horizontal navigation arrangement as normal size, although two labels no longer fit and the keyboard control becomes the largest shell icon.
deductions.impact: The common navigation system loses readable destination identity in both selected-page states. This system-level deduction concerns the shared adaptation strategy; T1 records the label-level legibility defect.

deductions.observation: At AX5, navigation, result-count copy, and composer icons grow sharply while filter glyphs, row menus, and People initials retain approximately their normal visual scale.
deductions.impact: The two pages remain related, but their control and metadata scaling no longer presents a coherent accessibility layout. This does not establish tap-target or VoiceOver compliance.

corrections.change: Adapt the shared shell for accessibility sizes: retain complete destination labels, arrange count/preview as supporting metadata, and make the composer and its glyphs proportionate while preserving the chosen text size and all commands.
corrections.verification: Capture both pages at AX5 again, then verify page navigation, search, filter, and composer commands on the running app. Full destination labels must remain readable, and the shell should not dominate the first record.

corrections.change: Give People identity a full-width layout at accessibility sizes, placing initials so they do not constrain the name or split a surname.
corrections.verification: Capture AX5 with short, long, and multiword names. Names must remain whole-word readable and grouped consistently with role/company and search context; scrolling can accommodate height.

corrections.change: Make unread independently recognizable from Review needed, using a restrained, explicit read-state cue while retaining a separate operational-attention label.
corrections.verification: Show read/unread crossed with review-needed/not-needed in light and dark. A new reviewer should identify both states independently; separately exercise the actual read-state transition and persistence.

missing_proof: Search and filter behavior on both pages
Reset and recovery from empty results
Page navigation and complete content access at AX5
functional_gates.note: Visual score is a subjective craft judgment and cannot outweigh a failed functional gate or establish real recruiter usefulness.
